To abolish synthesis of the anti-nutritional compound we want a mutation that knocks out, or at least severely cripples, the protein encoded by this gene.  
Among the four EMS-induced alleles we must see which one is most likely to inactivate the gene product.

1. Intact reading frame (first few codons):
   ATG-TTT-CTC-GCT-GGT-ACT-TCT … (Met-Phe-Leu-Ala-Gly-Thr-Ser …)

2. Mutant 1  
   ATG-TTC-TAC-GCT-GGT-ACT-TCT …  
   CTC → TAC changes Leu→Tyr (missense).  A single amino-acid change early in the protein is unlikely to guarantee complete loss of function.

3. Mutant 3  
   ATG-TTT-TAC-GCT-GGT-GTC-ACT-TCT …  
   Two missense changes (Leu→Tyr and Thr→Val) but the reading frame is intact; no early stop codon.  Function may be retained.

4. Mutant 4  
   ATG-TTT-TAC-GCT-ACT-TCT …  
   A 3-nt in-frame deletion removes one Gly residue but leaves the rest of the protein intact; activity could persist.

5. Mutant 2  
   ATG-TTC-TAA-GCT …  
   The third codon has become TAA, an in-frame nonsense (STOP) codon.  
   • Translation terminates after only two amino acids, producing no functional enzyme.  
   • Because the premature stop is >50 nt upstream of the first exon–exon junction, the mRNA will be targeted by nonsense-mediated decay, further lowering any protein production.

This early nonsense mutation therefore has by far the highest probability of abolishing the enzyme that synthesises the anti-nutritional compound.

Answer: D
